subject: Sunrise pilot — DPA transfers, subprocessors & prompt/response ownership
messages:
From: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@sunrisehealth.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@sunrisehealth.com, david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Pilot DPA questions — training carveouts & transfer lanes

Hi Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the Sunrise pilot team is excited to move forward. Before procurement signs the SOW we need to close a few items in the DPA you sent:

1) No-training/Model improvement: Our security team requires an explicit "no-training" commitment for pilot data and an operational proofflow for that (how you enforce, where traces/logs live, and a small-sample audit path). Can you confirm Redwood will not use pilot prompts/responses for model updates (including internal CI training pipelines) and provide a short ops description we can include in the DPA?

2) Prompt/response ownership: We need language that confirms Sunrise retains IP in prompts and generated responses and that Redwood will not claim derivative rights beyond delivering the output to us.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: Please provide the current subprocessors list and clarify which locations could see pilot data (cloud regions, any third-party analytics). Also confirm the export lanes (SFTP/API) we discussed and whether onshore KMS is available for pilot keys.

I've attached a single redline doc (Sunrise_DPA_redlines_v1.docx) and a subprocessor matrix for context.

Can we get a short written reply by EOD Wednesday Nov 4 for procurement's deadline? If needed, procurement can loop in legal but wanted to try to resolve operationally first.

Best,
Elena Rodriguez
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Sunrise Health

Attachment: Sunrise_DPA_redlines_v1.docx (docx, 45KB)
Attachment: subprocessor_matrix_v2.csv (csv, 8KB)

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Pilot DPA questions — training carveouts & transfer lanes

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Short answers up front, then a proposed ops writeup below:

- No-training: Yes — Redwood will commit to a no-training (no-model-improvement) obligation for all data scoped in the pilot SOW. That includes prompt/responses and telemetry generated during pilot sessions.
- Ownership: Sunrise retains ownership of prompts and generated outputs; Redwood will provide only the delivery/serving rights needed to operate the service.
- Subprocessors & transfers: Current subprocessors are listed in the attached matrix; pilot traffic will remain in the US region unless you opt into APAC/EU nodes. We support SFTP export and API-based export; onshore KMS (US) can be offered for pilot keys.

Below is an ops blurb you can paste into the DPA as an appendix (we'll also formalize for legal):

"No-training operational controls (pilot):
- Data scope: Pilot inputs and generated outputs are tagged with the pilot identifier and excluded from all model-improvement pipelines.
- Runtime controls: Model-serving paths are segmented for pilot sessions; any telemetry that reaches long-term stores is redacted and labelled non-trainable.
- Auditability: We maintain an audit log of all pilot sessions (IDs, timestamps, and export actions). Upon request we provide an export extract and a short attestation showing exclusion from training queues.
- Subprocessors: Any access by subprocessors to pilot data is limited by contract and logged; the current matrix is provided for review.
"

I'll loop legal if you need contractual text changes, but hope this helps procurement. Happy to set a quick 20-min call tomorrow if you want to walk through the ops details.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP, Product & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Elena — adding the legal perspective and a few suggested clauses to address procurement's ask. I've attached a marked-up DPA (Sunrise_DPA_redlines_v1.docx) and included extract language below. High-level notes: we can commit to the pilot-specific no-training language but need clear scoping (pilot SOW name, time window, and data tags). We also prefer operational attestation + logs vs. warranty-heavy wording.

Suggested DPA insert (draft):
"Section X.X — Pilot no-model-improvement commitment
1. Scope: For the duration of the Pilot (defined in the SOW), Provider (Redwood) shall not use Customer Data (including prompts, uploads, transcripts, and generated outputs) to train, fine-tune, evaluate, or otherwise improve any machine learning models ("No-Train Commitment").
2. Operational controls: Provider shall implement and maintain technical and administrative measures reasonably designed to ensure exclusion of Pilot Data from training pipelines, including but not limited to (a) dataset tagging and segmentation, (b) access controls, and (c) exclusion flags at ingestion and storage layers.
3. Audit and attestation: Upon Customer's reasonable request, Provider will provide a snapshot extract and a written attestation confirming that Pilot Data was excluded from training queues for the period specified in the SOW.
4. Subprocessors: Provider shall ensure contractual obligations on subprocessors to conform to this Section and shall provide Customer with the subprocessor list and data center regions in scope for the Pilot.
"

Other items to confirm in redline:
- If Sunrise requires onshore (US) KMS for pilot keys we can add an addendum for key custody and rotation.
- For prompt/response IP, we've added a short sentence preserving customer ownership and restricting derivative rights to the minimum required to provide the service.

Next steps:
- If Sunrise accepts this draft language, legal can prepare a clean DPA update quickly.
- If procurement wants stronger contractual remedies, flag which clauses and we'll escalate internally.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Sunrise_DPA_redlines_v1.docx (marked-up with clause suggestions)

Thanks Markus / Kimberly — this is helpful and closer to what procurement/legal needs. A couple of follow-ups before we sign:

1) Attestation cadence: Procurement wants an attestation within 30 days after pilot end and one interim attestation if the pilot runs longer than 90 days. Can you confirm you can do both?
2) Subprocessor detail: The matrix lists a third-party analytics provider (InsightMetrics) that does anonymized telemetry processing. Please confirm: does InsightMetrics ever receive raw prompts or only aggregated telemetry? We need a one-sentence attestation.
3) Onshore KMS: Sunrise prefers provider-managed onshore KMS for pilot keys; if Redwood cannot provide managed onshore keys for the pilot, we need a documented handoff procedure for customer-supplied keys.

Procurement's timeline is tight — they need a clear yes/no on the attestation cadence and the InsightMetrics scope by EOD Thursday Nov 4.

Elena

Elena — quick update to meet procurement's deadline:

1) Attestations: Yes — Redwood can provide (a) an interim attestation at 90 days if the pilot exceeds 90 days, and (b) a final attestation within 30 days after pilot termination. We will include timelines in the SOW.

2) InsightMetrics: Confirmed — InsightMetrics receives only aggregated telemetry (metrics and event counts). They do NOT receive raw prompts or generated outputs for the pilot. We will add the following attestation sentence to the DPA: 
"Provider confirms that, for the Pilot scope specified in the SOW, InsightMetrics will only process aggregated telemetry and will not receive raw prompts or generated outputs. Provider will maintain contractual restrictions on InsightMetrics to prevent re-identification or use for model training."

3) KMS: We can support provider-managed onshore KMS for the pilot. If Sunrise prefers to manage keys, we can accept customer-supplied keys under a documented handoff process; we'll add a KMS addendum to the SOW.

Next steps: I will ask legal to prepare a clean DPA update (with the draft insert Kimberly supplied) and produce a short ops attestation template. Expect: clean DPA + attestation template + updated subprocessor matrix by Friday EOD PST.

If procurement/legal at Sunrise can sign off on that package we can proceed to countersign the SOW next week.

Thanks — marking as resolved pending your confirmation.

Regards,
Markus Klein
VP, Product & Partnerships
